description: WinuxCmd release pin for niubash releases (niubash#312). Tag-push releases bundle exactly this WinuxCmd tag: the workflow downloads the matching WinuxCmd-*-win-<arch>.zip asset and fails unless its SHA-256 equals the value recorded here. workflow_dispatch releases must instead pass the same information explicitly via the winuxcmd_tag and winuxcmd_sha256 inputs; this file is then only the reference for what the last pinned release used.
notes: Recorded from WinuxCmd v1.1.18 (2026-10-20); values taken from the v1.1.18 GitHub Release asset digests and wpm-source index entry.
The hashes cover the WinuxCmd-<version>-win-<arch>.zip release assets (the only format the release bundles), not the .7z/.tar.gz/setup.exe variants.
Bumping the pin is a deliberate release decision: update winuxcmd_tag and both sha256 values together, and rerun a release so the bundled engine changes intentionally.

History: v1.1.13 = first release where a forced upgrade completes while a running git holds the payload; v1.1.14 shipped the layout:shim forwarder's code without the binary; v1.1.15 = first zip verifiably carrying winuxcmd-shim.exe (WinuxCmd#1207/#1225); v1.1.16 carries the POSIX drive-dialect fixes for mkdir/ln/stat/realpath/readlink (WinuxCmd#1233/#1235/#1241/#1245); v1.1.18 suppresses orphan console window creation in winuxcmd-shim.exe when the parent has no visible console (WinuxCmd#1282, niubash#466).

Pending floor (niubash#467): the bundled gawk payload is a text-mode mingw build — the LF contract on its stdin/stdout/stderr ships in the forwarder's adapted-command argv splice (`-v BINMODE=3` for awk/gawk), which no release up to and including v1.1.18 carries. The next pin bump must move to the first WinuxCmd release containing that adapter; the staged verify's raw-byte awk probes fail the x64 gate until then.
